title: Arjuna asks to see
hook: the greatest archer asks for his chariot between the armies, to get a good look at the enemy, and Krishna parks it in front of his grandfather
carry: the charioteer showed him: the enemy is family

segments.voice: Yesterday, the armies: a blind king asking, conch shells roaring. Your line was every life is a field of dharma. Today, Arjuna asks for one thing, and gets it.

The conches have finished roaring. Arrows are about to fly. Arjuna, the archer, lifts his bow. Over his chariot flies his banner, and on it is Hanuman, the monkey who carried a mountain, the one you met on this path. Arjuna turns to his driver, Krishna, with a perfectly sensible request: drive me out between the two armies, so I can see who I'm fighting. Any good commander would do it. Size up the other side. Krishna says nothing. He just drives.
screen: `HANUMAN ON THE BANNER.` → `DRIVE ME OUT BETWEEN THEM.` → `KRISHNA JUST DRIVES.`

segments.voice: In Sanskrit, Arjuna's request is: senayor ubhayor madhye ratham sthapaya me 'chyuta. Between both armies, set my chariot, Achyuta, unfailing one. He wants to see, he says, those who've come to fight for Duryodhana. He's thinking of enemies. Now watch where Krishna stops. Sanjaya tells the king: Krishna drove between the armies and set the chariot down right in front of Bhishma and Drona. Bhishma, the great-uncle Arjuna grew up calling grandfather. Drona, the teacher who taught him to shoot. Of all the places on that huge field, Krishna parks there. And he says one line, his first words in the whole Gita: Partha, look at these Kurus, gathered together. Arjuna looks. The text slows down and lists what he sees, one by one: fathers, grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, friends, fathers-in-law. Every one of them is family, or nearly. He asked to see the enemy, and he saw his people. The verse says he was overcome with pity, and he began to speak, in sorrow. Krishna doesn't argue, warn or explain. He just puts Arjuna where he'll have to see the truth. Hindus love this picture: Krishna as Parthasarathi, Arjuna's charioteer, and many homes and temples show it. Arjuna holds the bow; God holds the reins. A fight looks easy from a distance, where the other side is a category: them. Stop in front of real faces, and the category falls apart. Everything the Gita says next starts here.
screen: `SET MY CHARIOT BETWEEN THE ARMIES.` · `KRISHNA STOPS BEFORE BHISHMA, DRONA.` · `PARTHA, LOOK AT THEM.` · `ARJUNA HOLDS THE BOW. GOD HOLDS THE REINS.` · then, large: `THE ENEMY IS FAMILY.`

segments.voice: Think of someone on the other side of something with you, at work, at home, in the news, someone who's become a category in your mind: them. Picture Krishna driving your chariot out and stopping right in front of their face, and wonder who raised them, who they're a father, a sister, a grandchild to, what they looked like at ten. You don't have to agree with them; just look, and let them be a person for a minute.
Achyuta, the unfailing one Arjuna calls Krishna when he asks to see his chariot set between the two armies. Krishna stops it in front of the people he loves.
Your line: the charioteer showed him: the enemy is family. Arjuna has seen; now he has to speak. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Readers of the Gita often pause on 1.21–1.27, where Krishna drives Arjuna's chariot between the armies and stops before Bhishma and Drona; some readers hear Krishna's first words, telling Arjuna to look, as the quiet start of all that follows.

Achyuta.meaning: the unfailing one; a name for Krishna

Bhishma.meaning: Arjuna's great-uncle, whom he called grandfather

Drona.meaning: the teacher who taught Arjuna archery

Partha.meaning: son of Pritha; a name for Arjuna

Parthasarathi.meaning: Arjuna's charioteer: a name for Krishna

sources.quoted: senayor ubhayor madhye ratham sthapaya me 'chyuta

notes: Hanuman on Arjuna's banner (kapidhvaja), 1.20. Confirm the tie-back to the Hanuman week (days 29–35).
Krishna 'sets it down in front of Bhishma and Drona and all the kings' (1.25). Confirm.

Krishna's first words in the Gita, 1.25: 'Partha, behold these Kurus gathered together'; paraphrased as 'look at these Kurus, gathered together'. Confirm the claim they are his first words (he blows his conch in 1.14 but does not speak).
Achyuta glossed as 'unshakable one' (lit. 'the unfallen'). Confirm.
